name: Publius
title: The Leading Man on Malta
summary: Publius was the foremost man (the chief official) on the island of Malta when the apostle Paul was shipwrecked there. He welcomed Paul and his companions hospitably for three days, and his father was healed by Paul from fever and dysentery, which led to many other sick people on the island also being healed.

keyEvents.title: Paul's Shipwreck on Malta
keyEvents.description: After a dramatic shipwreck in the Mediterranean Sea, Paul and everyone on board safely reached the island of Malta, where Publius was the leading official.

keyEvents.title: Publius Welcomes Paul Hospitably
keyEvents.description: Publius kindly received Paul and his companions, giving them shelter for three days, showing remarkable hospitality to the shipwrecked.

keyEvents.title: The Healing of Publius' Father
keyEvents.description: Publius' father lay sick with fever and dysentery. Paul went in to him, prayed, laid hands on him, and healed him.

keyEvents.title: More Healings on Malta
keyEvents.description: After the healing of Publius' father, other sick people on the island also came to Paul and were healed, leading to great gratitude among the people.

keyEvents.title: The Generosity of the Maltese
keyEvents.description: As a result of the healings and the example set by Publius, the people of Malta showed great honor to Paul and his companions, supplying them with everything they needed as they continued their journey.
